title: What Reactive Everything Is
definition: Reactive Everything: systems where everything reacts to change.
description:
Strip Reactive Everything to its essence and you get systems where everything reacts to change. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Software Paradigms: first signal graphs understanding, then system logistics prototypes, then glitch freedom operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of system hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

title: Real Research Today: Reactive Everything
definition: Today's documented research behind Reactive Everything.
description:
The road to Reactive Everything is already being paved. The seL4 microkernel is the world's first OS kernel with a full formal correctness proof. Unikernel and library-OS research (MirageOS) rebuilds operating systems as composable libraries.

Projectional editing (JetBrains MPS) lets languages reshape the editor itself. Together these programs form the signal graphs foundation that Reactive Everything will build on — the system logistics results, the glitch freedom methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Reactive Everything
definition: Estimates Reactive Everything readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Reactive Everything components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Reactive Everything Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Reactive Everything operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Reactive Everything installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 33395 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where signal graphs monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or glitch freedom maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Reactive Everything Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Reactive Everything: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Reactive Everything — systems where everything reacts to change.

Phase 1 — Prove (signal graphs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (glitch freedom): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (time semantics): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and developers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
